title: Built a fully automated crypto trading system. Curious what you think of the results.
author: According-Ad-2638
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/bh2yxkqgnx0i1.png

Hey everyone,

I've been working on an automated crypto trading system for quite a while, covering BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP.

It's fully autonomous, handling everything from signal generation and position sizing to risk management and execution. No manual trading decisions.

My main focus has always been risk management rather than trying to predict every market move.

I've attached a performance report covering Feb 2025 to Sep 2026, including a comparison with an equal-weight buy-and-hold portfolio of the same four coins.

The trading records come from real trading, not just a backtest. The report also looks at performance using volatility-scaled position sizing.

I'm curious what people here think of the results, especially from a risk management perspective.

I'm also exploring opportunities to move into institutional quant research or systematic trading. My background is in ML research, software development, and trading, though I haven't followed the traditional quant career path.

Would this kind of work be relevant to a prop firm or a quant trading team?

Interested to hear your thoughts.

comments.author: Either-Nobody-3962
comments.body:
did you do only longs or shorts too?  
and whats the selection criteria for coin n entry.

replies.author: According-Ad-2638
replies.body:
Both long and short. I focus on BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP, mainly for their liquidity.

The system handles entries, position sizing, and risk management automatically, evaluating the market tick by tick.

I'd rather keep the exact entry logic private, but happy to discuss the general approach.

replies.author: Either-Nobody-3962
replies.body:
I did many backtests n all came out to be coin flip n at end Ai said, human eye n our decision/6th sense/gut feeling to enter or not makes while difference.
But seems you nailed it. 

On avg, how many trades it takes a day

replies.author: According-Ad-2638
replies.body:
Thanks, appreciate it!

About 0.5 closed trades per day across all four coins, so roughly one every two days.

The system evaluates the market tick by tick, but only trades when the conditions are met. No manual decisions involved.

replies.author: Either-Nobody-3962
replies.body: OK, so you must have found your edge n wrote strict rules

replies.author: According-Ad-2638
replies.body: Pretty much, yeah. The real challenge for me was turning the research into a system that could actually trade on its own, with risk management built in. That's where I've spent most of my time.

replies.author: According-Ad-2638
replies.body:
It's actually live trading with real capital, not a backtest or paper trading. The system hasn't been changed at all since February 2025.

And yeah, u/Either-Nobody-3962 got it right. Thanks to both of you for taking a look!

comments.author: DatGiantIsopod
comments.body:
They're some pretty tasty results so far.

In general terms - is it a swing trading model? In backtest what max drawdown did you get? Because your Calmar for live trading so far is pretty excellent for crypto.

I have a crypto set-up I'm running small position live now with a similar sort of Calmar in backtest but I'm not really expecting the same for live since some will obvs be due to overfitting. Currently playing around with position sizing and so on. Any general tips you can share for that side of things?

replies.author: According-Ad-2638
replies.body:
Thanks, appreciate it!

It's a fully automated, tick-driven system. Holding periods vary, but average around 5.5 days, so it's closer to swing trading than day trading.

I don't use backtest results to tune the system. The numbers in the report are from live trading, and the drawdown shown is based on closed trades, not mark-to-market.

For position sizing, I'd say start with how much risk you're comfortable taking, not how much profit you're hoping to make. I focus on managing exposure and adjusting position sizes based on market conditions rather than using a fixed size for every trade.

To me, risk management matters more than trying to predict every market move.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
About 19 months live is a decent start, but BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP are very correlated, so it's closer to one big crypto bet than four independent ones. I'd regress the daily returns on the equal-weight basket to see how much is just being net long crypto at the right times.

If you pitch it to a prop firm or quant team, they'll probably ask for trade count and the results split by long vs short and by coin first. If one side or one coin carries most of it, better you find that before they do.

replies.author: According-Ad-2638
replies.body:
Good points, thanks for the advice.

Yeah, the four coins are pretty correlated. But I also chose them to spread execution across different order books, not just for diversification. That matters more as capital grows.

The system manages overall exposure and risk across all four, so I don't treat them as independent bets.

And you're right about breaking down the results by long/short and by coin. Definitely worth looking at, especially if I'm presenting this to a prop firm or quant team. Appreciate the input!
